title: adaptive-prefetch-oracle-and-quant-stability-scoring
author: Priya Ramanathan
description:
Motivation: Improve default prefetch and quantization choices by using telemetry-driven prefetch hints and a lightweight stability scoring model for quant profiles. Many tenants see regressions after aggressive 4-bit/INT8 quant promotions; operators currently rely on manual holdouts and expensive evals. This change introduces an "Adaptive Prefetch Oracle" that synthesizes short-term workload signals (prefix reuse, KV cache hit rates, sequence length distribution) into per-tenant prefetch hints, and a companion "Quant Stability Scorer" that predicts risk of quality regressions for a given model+quant profile using a tuned feature set and a small offline eval sampler.

What this PR does (in brief):
- Adds telemetry ingestion and feature extraction pipeline for short-window prefetch signals.
- Implements the Prefetch Oracle service with a gRPC and CLI endpoint that returns prefetch hints (none/minimal/normal/greedy) per tenant + route.
- Introduces a compact quant stability scoring module (Python + Rust FFI) that outputs a stability score and recommended guardrail flags (disable extreme quant, enable fallback variant).
- Exposes a dry-run CLI and a dashboard hook for operators to simulate unit economics impact before applying presets.
- Adds unit and integration tests, plus a small benchmark harness to measure false-positive/false-negative rates of stability predictions.

Design/engineering notes: The stability scorer intentionally sacrifices absolute recall to avoid blocking low-risk quant upgrades; we tune to favor precision because false positives (blocking a quant upgrade) are recoverable via manual promotion, while false negatives (silent regressions) are costly. The scorer uses a small set of features engineered from eval diffs, token-level perplexity drifts on held-out golden prompts, and telemetry-derived context-switch metrics. The Rust FFI provides low-latency scoring in the hot path and is exercised in unit tests.

Backward compatibility: Prefetch hints default to existing legacy behavior if the oracle is disabled. Quant scoring returns an explicit "unknown" status when insufficient telemetry exists, preserving current autopromotion flows.

Migration: No DB schema changes. New telemetry metrics are emitted under the "prefetch_oracle.*" namespace; downstream dashboards auto-pick them up. Ops runbook included for emergency rollback.

Notes about uniqueness: This PR combines a short-window telemetry-driven prefetch advisor with a quant-stability prediction component and a dry-run unit-economics estimator — a different approach from prior purely heuristic defaults or offline quant profiles. The aim is to reduce operator toil and reduce post-quantization quality incidents while still enabling safe cost wins.

Release notes: "Introduce Adaptive Prefetch Oracle and Quant Stability Scorer: pilot feature that provides tenant-aware prefetch hints and predicts quantization regressions. Includes a dry-run CLI for cost impact analysis and dashboard panels for monitoring."
